caption: Funerals cost more than most policies cover. What did the last one in your family really cost?

slides.title:
Where my R29 000
went the month
my gran passed
Living in Humansdorp
slides.body:
Male, 28
Single, no kids
Job: Wind farm technician
Net salary: R29 000 p/m

slides.title: Funeral costs
slides.includes: Tombstone deposit, catering, a cow, my share of the tent
slides.body: Her policy covered the coffin only. The family split the rest and I put in more than my share.

slides.title: Rent
slides.body: It's R1 000 less than Jeffreys Bay and a twenty minute drive.

slides.title: Fuel & car
slides.body: I drove to Mthatha twice in one month. R1 800 in petrol alone.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.body: I mostly ate what was left over at the funeral.

slides.title: Eating out
slides.body: This one has nothing to do with grief and everything to do with not cooking.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Prepaid electricity, phone, medical aid, funeral policy, stokvel, black tax, gym
slides.body: Every other line was on autopilot. If you ask what happened this month, I'd say only the funeral.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R29 000. I went into overdraft for two days before payday and I'm still not sure which line did it.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded the month's statement to Beyond Horizon and saw the exact day the account went red.

It was the day I paid the tombstone deposit.

No bank login needed.
